analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/qwen-mtp-concurrent-decode.md, lines 1-5) and an added paragraph in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~1116-1128). No executable source was supplied, so the implementation is unreviewed. The docs describe Qwen inline MTP head changes: ordinary chained decode while more than one request decodes, hidden rows appended to the assistant history in step order, and a carry stored once no successor is in flight. The final prompt row's hidden state seeds the first speculative round. Two rollback env switches are described, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY, and the changelog notes LaunchAgents do not forward them.

The docs make no claim that weakens a threat-model control. They do not touch the encrypted prefix cache or SSD tier (T-041), attestation, authorization, or key handling. Still unverified, for a pass that sees the code (EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift, finalizeMTPOrdinaryHistory):
- Per-request isolation of the assistant history and carry state across concurrent requests, which touches A-001 and the cross-tenant concern in T-041/T-028.
- Whether the carry state is correctly checkpointed or invalidated when SSD recurrent prefix reuse or cancellation intervenes.
- Whether the removal of the policy top-two reduction affects constrained decoding or tool-choice constraints.

The env switches are local rollback knobs in the same class as the existing DARKBLOOM_CBV2_MTP kill switch. I found no regression or new attack surface from these docs alone.
